texts: mixed: the moon, its fullness and Year 2 are all recorded faithfully, but "day 540" lands in the translator's day-of-month slot, which it reads as a 1-31 day inside a month, so this date cannot be ordered against "day 555" in the next episode. If you want episode dates to compare, give the day a month-sized division to sit in: "On the twelfth day of Greenmoon, Year 2, the moon was full.", substituting whatever your calendar calls that division. Left as written the sentence itself loses nothing; only date ordering does.
good. the convening, the Council as the one convening and the Watch as its location all land, and both capitalized labels are correctly kept as ordinary common nouns rather than proper names.

bad: the report, its speaker and its addressee are right, but "twelve weeks of supply" is recorded as the supply itself having a twelve-week duration, a dimension no word in the sentence supplies, and the only compliant alternative records a bare "12 weeks" with no statement of what the weeks measure. Put the lasting on a verb instead: "Sailsworn reported to the Council that the salt-bloom store's supply would last twelve weeks." A duration stated of an eventuality is licensed, so this keeps the time-to-exhaustion reading exactly.

bad: the same problem as the salt-bloom report, "five weeks of supply" becomes a five-week duration of the supply itself, a dimension the sentence never states. Rewrite as "Tessa Brae reported to the Council that the feather store's supply would last five weeks." Everything else here (speaker, addressee, the store and its genus) already parses cleanly.

mixed: the Council, the doubled ration, the station and the continuing all land, but "through the spring" becomes an interval END at spring, i.e. the ration stopped when spring arrived, rather than a span running across it. "Throughout" is one of the three words the translator reads as a span, so write: "The Council continued the doubled feather ration at the Stilllight Station throughout the spring."

bad: "more thoroughly" is dropped entirely, because a comparative with nothing to compare against has no licensed form, so the parse says only that the Council asked for feather collection in the molting season. Supply the standard and the comparison becomes expressible: "The Council asked the apprentices to collect feathers more thoroughly in the molting season than they had in the previous molting season." Separately, nothing records whom the Council asked (the apprentices appear only as the collectors), but that one is a translator-side gap no rewrite of yours can fix.

bad: the third instance of the same measure problem, "eight months of supply" lands as an eight-month duration of the supply, a dimension no word supplies. Rewrite as "Hesper reported to the Council that the mire-essence reserve's supply would last eight months." The reserve, its genus, and the report's speaker and addressee are all already correct.

good. the saying is treated as non-factive so nothing about the harvest is asserted as fact, the indefinite harvest stays inside the report, "would" is recorded as future relative to the saying, and "the reserve" is correctly resolved to the mire-essence reserve of the previous sentence.
